name: Eyes on Earth — Boundary Score Benchmark
description: Boundary test fixture: target exactly 30.0% overall score. Tests the threshold boundary rule where a score of exactly 30.0% passes the score threshold alone. Documents the mathematical conditions required to hit 30.0% alongside the specific backend blocker regarding discrete versus continuous scoring.

scoreCalculationDetails.structureContribution: 20% weight * 50.0 (bus-reinforced heavily penalised for 2-yr LEO/SSO mission) = 10.00
scoreCalculationDetails.instrumentContribution: 25% weight * 40.0 (optical camera attenuated by comms/orbit delivery mismatch) = 10.00
scoreCalculationDetails.orbitContribution: 15% weight * 0.0 (unreachable orbit trajectory zeroes orbit score) = 0.00
scoreCalculationDetails.launcherContribution: 15% weight * 0.0 (incompatible launcher assignment zeroes launcher score) = 0.00
scoreCalculationDetails.passFailVerdict: Score is exactly 30.00% -> PASSES the score threshold (>= 30%). However, feasibility FAILS due to orbit/launcher incompatibility (FC-6) and telemetry deficit (FC-5).

blockerDocumentation: BLOCKER: Vineeth has not yet implemented continuous mathematical penalty functions in scoring.service.ts. Under the current discrete lookup table in component-suitability.json, individual component base ratings fall into fixed values (40, 50, 70, 75, 80, 85, 90, 95). A fully feasible spacecraft using those discrete values mathematically cannot score below 68.75%. To achieve an exact 30.00% score on a fully feasible design, the backend developer must specify continuous degradation curves (e.g. fractional scaling based on margin ratios). Without those confirmed curves, an exact 30.00% can only be demonstrated by applying trajectory/comms zeroing as modeled above.
